assessments.reasoning: The publisher's HTTPS receipt matches the claim's 1.1 revision and edition path. The heading “LPPL Version 1.1  1999-07-10” independently identifies the publisher side.
Four contiguous ranges cover the 61,351-byte detail in SPDX's pinned tree. Part 3 gives “LaTeX Project Public License v1.1”, licenseId LPPL-1.1, and both HTTP citations.
The official repository's unsigned annotated tag v3.29.0 identifies its target as a commit with SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. That exact commit appears in the 1.1 detail locator.

challenge.method: Distinguished the URL in the sample license notice from the detail's crossRef and seeAlso. Checked licenseId, release target, date, and representation differences.
challenge.results: The example uses the generic /lppl.txt path. Both citation fields use /lppl/lppl-1-1.txt and crossRef records match as “false”. SPDX licenseText joins “The latest version of this license is in % http://www.latex-project.org/lppl.txt” on one line. The publisher places the URL on the next comment line.

limitations: The schemes differ. The finding covers SPDX's edition citation only. Byte equivalence, legal equivalence, application to a work, and redistribution rights require separate evidence.
reasoning: The SPDX 3.29.0 detail lists LPPL-1.1 and cites http://www.latex-project.org/lppl/lppl-1-1.txt. The publisher capture at https://www.latex-project.org/lppl/lppl-1-1.txt names edition 1.1 at the same host and path.
